caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 470 of 1998.
lawyer:
For the petitioners Mr. Sharif Uddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record. 
For respondent No. 1: Mr. Nurul Huq, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr. A.K.M. Shahidul Hoque, Advocate-on-Record. 
Respondent No. 2: Not represented.
parties:
Lokman Fakir and others ------ Petitioners.
Versus
Abdul Jabbar Bayati & Ors ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mohammad Abdur Rouf, J.: Late Wazed All Fakir, father of the present petitioners instituted Partition Suit No. 424 of 1980 in the First Court of Munsif, Madaripur praying for partition in respect of 3.24 acres of land impleading the pre-sent defendant No. 1 as defendant No. 5. The suit was, however, renumbered as Title Suit No. 22 of 1983 of the Court of the Assistant Judge, Rajoir. During pendency of that suit the said plaintiff came to know about the ex-parte decree dated 20.5.84 passed in Title Suit No. 564 of 1983, instituted by defendant No. 1, for specific performance of contract, by fabricating a binapatra said to have been executed by the said plaintiff in favour of the said defendant No. 1 and that the summons of the suit was not served upon the said plaintiff. Thus plaintiff then instituted Title Suit No. 117 of 1984 in question in the Court of Assistant Judge. Rajoir, District Madaripur for declaration that the aforesaid ex-parte decree is fraudulent, void and not binding upon him etc. 

 2. Defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement asserting, inter alia, that the decree in question is not a fraudulent one, that the plaintiff Wazed Ali sold the suit land to him by executing a binapatra on 5th Falgun, 1377 B.S. for Tk. 4000/- and on receipt of Tk. 3800/- handed over possession thereof but he subsequently refused to execute the required kabala and thereby he filed the aforesaid suit and got the relevant kabala on 29.7.84 through court, in Title Execution Case No. 8 of 1984. 

 3. The trial court by judgment and decree dated 30.6.87 dismissed the Suit. The plaintiff then preferred Title Appeal No. 290 of 1987 against the said decree of the trial court. A learned Subordinate Judge, Madaripur by judgment and decree dated 9.4.90 allowed the appeal and after setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial court decreed the suit declaring that the decree obtained by defendant No. 1 in Title Suit No. 564 of 1983 is void, illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff. Against the said judgment and decree of the lower appellate court, defendant No. 1 moved the High Court Division under Section 115 of Code of Civil Procedure and obtained a Rule, Civil Revision No. 1116 of 1990. A learned Single Judge of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order dated 10.11.97 upon making the Rule absolute set aside the decree of the lower appellate court and restored that of the trial court and there-by the suit has been dismissed. 

 6. It appears that the trial court on consideration of the oral evidence on record, the content of Ext. and other documents held that on the refusal to receive the summons of the said suit by said Wazed Ali Fakir, the same was served by hanging and in accordance with law in presence of mokabela wit-nesses namely, D.Ws. 4 and 5. but the lower appellate court without considering the evidence of those mokabela witnesses wrongly held that the summons were not properly served upon defendant No. 1 of that suit. The learned Judge of the High Court Division having, thus found fault with the appellate court's judgment, in our opinion, rightly set aside the judgment and decree of the lower appellate court in exercise of his revisional authority. Thus we find no merit in this petition.
